title: Geometry - Lesson 2 Assessment: Formal Quadrilateral Classification
description: Show mastery by classifying quadrilaterals from definitions, properties, hierarchy, and written evidence.

questions.question: Which set of properties guarantees that a quadrilateral is a square?
options: Exactly one pair of parallel sides
Four right angles and four congruent sides
Two pairs of adjacent congruent sides
Two pairs of parallel sides only
questions.explanation: A square has both rectangle properties and rhombus properties: four right angles and four congruent sides.

questions.question: A quadrilateral has four congruent sides, but no right angles are given. What is the most specific classification guaranteed?
options: Rectangle
Rhombus
Square
Trapezoid only
questions.explanation: Four congruent sides guarantee a rhombus. A square would also require right-angle evidence.

questions.question: Which statement best explains the quadrilateral hierarchy?
options: A square belongs only to the square category.
A rectangle cannot be a parallelogram.
A square is a special rectangle and a special rhombus.
A kite must always be a rectangle.
questions.explanation: A square satisfies the definitions of square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, and quadrilateral.

questions.question: A shape that looks like a diamond is automatically a rhombus.
questions.explanation: A rhombus must have four congruent sides. The drawing's appearance is not enough proof.

questions.question: A parallelogram with four right angles is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A rectangle is a parallelogram with four right angles.

questions.question: Which property best distinguishes a kite from a rhombus?
options: A kite has no sides.
A kite has exactly three right angles.
A kite has two distinct pairs of adjacent congruent sides, while a rhombus has all four sides congruent.
A kite always has two pairs of opposite parallel sides.
questions.explanation: A kite is based on adjacent congruent side pairs. A rhombus has all four sides congruent and is a parallelogram.

questions.question: A quadrilateral has diagonals that bisect each other. What family is guaranteed by this property?
options: Parallelogram
Kite
Trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides
No quadrilateral family
questions.explanation: Diagonals that bisect each other are a standard parallelogram condition.

questions.question: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. Explain why it is not a parallelogram.
questions.correctAnswer: A parallelogram must have two pairs of parallel opposite sides. Exactly one pair of parallel sides makes it a trapezoid but not a parallelogram.
questions.explanation: The word exactly limits the parallel-side evidence to one pair, so the parallelogram definition is not satisfied.

questions.question: A quadrilateral has four right angles and side lengths 6 cm, 6 cm, 6 cm, and 6 cm. Give the most specific classification and one broader correct classification.
questions.correctAnswer: The most specific classification is square. A broader correct classification is rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, or quadrilateral.
questions.explanation: Four right angles and four congruent sides make a square. Since a square satisfies broader definitions, several broader classifications are also correct.

questions.question: A student says, "This quadrilateral is a rectangle because it looks like a window." Correct the reasoning.
questions.correctAnswer: The student needs geometric evidence, such as four right angles or a statement that it is a parallelogram with a right angle. Appearance alone does not prove rectangle.
questions.explanation: Formal classification must cite definitions, measurements, markings, or given statements rather than real-world appearance.
